# Wiki Page Types

The page-type catalog shared across sub-wikis. Each type sets a default authorship hedge; override only with reason. The *Default SLO* column is the last tier of the freshness precedence `wiki-page-freshness` §Resolution precedence states; base frontmatter lives in `wiki-page-spec`. **Sub-wiki** names the owning sub-wiki(s) — multiple values joined by `/`, owner first (e.g. `engineering/operations`) — and is the canonical, exhaustive mapping other documents (`wiki-federation-model`, the stage/process-keyed playbooks) point at rather than restate; it is a direct transcription of `wiki/_runtime/data/page-type-homes.json`, which drift-guards it against actual sub-wiki README content and playbook usage. The infra types (`redirect`, `index`, `log`) are universal — one per sub-wiki — rather than owned by one.

| Type | Purpose | Default authorship | Cadence | Register | Default SLO | Sub-wiki |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `concept` | Abstract idea or mental model | curated | living | explanatory | 365d | domain/product/design/operations/governance |
| `domain-object` | Named business concept in the shared domain vocabulary (Cart, Order, Invoice); the product logical-data-model flavor is `data-model-entity` | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | domain |
| `data-model-entity` | Product logical data-model entity — the `## Data model` table shape a feature's data acts on; distinct from the industry `domain-object` | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | product |
| `system-component` | Deployable, runnable, or persistent system thing — service, datastore, queue, cache, scheduled job (requires `realizes:`) | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | engineering |
| `system-entity` | The platform's own system/operational data — credentials, access grants, audit/telemetry, config; no customer-facing surface (internal admin/ops surfaces may exist). The engineering-side structural twin of the product `data-model-entity`; distinct from `system-component`, the runtime thing that stores it | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | engineering |
| `catalog` | Enumerated reference list of the members of a named, governed set — the canonical source other pages resolve a coded value against (a `concept`-filed enumeration retypes here with a frontmatter edit) | curated | living | explanatory | 365d | product/domain/design |
| `source-summary` | Summary of a single raw source | derived | record | explanatory | derived — none | domain |
| `interview-debrief` | JTBD four-forces debrief from a recent-switcher customer interview | derived | record | explanatory | derived — none | domain |
| `comparison` | Side-by-side of alternatives | derived | living | explanatory | 180d | domain |
| `adr` | Architecture decision record | canonical | record | explanatory | derived — none | engineering |
| `daci-record` | DACI-shaped strategic decision archive (Driver, Approver, Contributors, Informed roles + options considered + decision body + outcome) | canonical | record | explanatory | derived — none | governance |
| `synthesis` | Cross-source analysis | derived | living | explanatory | 180d | domain |
| `study` | First-party empirical investigation — spikes, benchmarks, manual tests, security audits — where raw artifacts are transient but findings are durable | derived | record | explanatory | derived — none | domain/design/engineering/governance |
| `architecture` | High-level system narrative — component topology, data-flow, boundary map, or deployment model | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | engineering |
| `workspace` | Where the artifacts of one tree live and where a new one goes — the layout of a repo or a governed content tree, and the placement decision for anything added to it (requires `kind`) | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | engineering |
| `test-scenario` | Test specification for one subject — scenarios, fixtures, and assertions traceable to what the subject declares; `tier` names the test level and with it the subject the page may verify — see the per-type required-field additions below | curated | living | explanatory | 90d | engineering |
| `ui-surface-impl` | Engineering build spec for a feature's surfaces — routing, view layer, data contract, and resilience states per surface | curated | living | explanatory | 90d | engineering |
| `api-contract` | Contract for an API resource — operations, request/response schemas, auth, errors, and versioning (protocol-neutral; REST by default) (requires `realizes:`) | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | engineering |
| `integration` | Technical spec for a third-party service dependency — protocol, auth and secrets, data exchanged, limits, and failure modes (requires `realizes:`) | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | engineering |
| `roadmap` | Product roadmap snapshot | canonical | living | explanatory | 30d | governance |
| `rice-round` | RICE prioritization round archive (candidate table + ranked output + decisions taken) | canonical | record | explanatory | derived — none | governance |
| `okr-cycle` | OKR cycle archive (Objective + KRs + cycle-end grading + retrospective) | canonical | record | explanatory | derived — none | governance |
| `pr-faq` | PR-FAQ archive (press release + FAQ + post-ship learnings) | canonical | record | persuasive | derived — none | product |
| `persona` | User persona | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | domain/product |
| `user-journey` | End-to-end experience arc a persona moves through across tasks/touchpoints | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | design |
| `ui-surface` | Per-feature visual and interaction spec, structured by named surface — layout intent, field inventory, states, and accessibility (any visual artifact is linked via `artifacts:`) | curated | living | explanatory | 90d | design |
| `ui-component` | Reusable UI component spec — anatomy, variants, states, props, behavior, and accessibility (requires `realizes:`) | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | design |
| `layout-pattern` | Page-arrangement spec — the regions of a page and their landmarks, the hierarchy, the arrangement at each width class, and where each navigation system sits; the shell of an application is one (requires `realizes:`, `platforms` and `kinds`) | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | design |
| `design-system` | Design-system overview — foundations and tokens, voice and tone, component index, interaction patterns, and governance (one per design wiki; any design-tool library linked) | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | design |
| `information-architecture` | Information architecture for a product scope — the sitemap table, navigation model, taxonomy and labeling, and wayfinding; a skeleton, a part or an application (requires `kind` and `platforms`) | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | design |
| `app-base` | Application base — the infrastructure no deliverable owns; the singleton page infra pages attribute to via `realizes:`; a `depends-on:` target | canonical | living | explanatory | 180d | product |
| `product-module` | A deliverable (application or library), an area of one, or a page describing shared content — a named grouping of related features (requires `audience` and `kind`; optionally supports `depends-on:`) | canonical | living | explanatory | 180d | product |
| `feature` | Committed feature description (use `concept` for speculative) (optionally supports `depends-on:`) | canonical | living | explanatory | 90d | product |
| `task-flow` | Ordered steps and task-scoped acceptance criteria for one task; input to design and integration tests | canonical | living | explanatory | 90d | product |
| `algorithm` | Domain-specific computation or algorithm definition — how a metric, index, or score is derived (requires `realizes:`) | canonical | living | explanatory | 180d | product |
| `mirror-source` | Summary + pointer to external canonical source | curated | living | explanatory | 30d | domain |
| `runbook` | Operational how-to | curated | living | explanatory | 90d | operations |
| `known-issue` | Documented quirk, limitation, scaling ceiling, or footgun with no fix yet | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | engineering |
| `campaign` | Marketing campaign / creative brief — objectives, audience, message, deliverables, channels, budget, metrics | curated | living | persuasive | 90d | gtm |
| `case-study` | Customer success story on the Challenge-Solution-Result arc — proof and testimonial | curated | living | persuasive | 365d | gtm |
| `competitor-profile` | Per-competitor profile and sales battlecard — positioning, strengths, weaknesses, why-we-win/lose, traps | curated | living | persuasive | 90d | gtm |
| `compliance-record` | Point-in-time, evidence-backed attestation that a control or requirement is satisfied for a defined scope, with accountable sign-off | canonical | record | explanatory | derived — none | operations |
| `incident-record` | What happened to the running system during a specific incident — impact, timeline, root cause, and the owned actions taken. A cycle or process retrospective is a `retrospective` instead | curated | record | explanatory | derived — none | operations |
| `operational-resource` | A vendor (contracted third party), environment (deployment target), or team (internal team/roster) the project depends on to run; `kind:` says which — the commercial/relationship, environment, or team record, distinct from the engineering `integration` technical spec | curated | living | explanatory | 90d | operations |
| `gtm-plan` | Go-to-market / launch plan — market opportunity, ICP, positioning, channels, timeline, goals | canonical | living | persuasive | 90d | gtm |
| `prd` | Product requirements document / brief — problem, evidence, success metrics, prioritized requirements, out-of-scope | canonical | living | explanatory | 180d | product |
| `pricing-model` | Pricing and packaging — value metric, tiers, rationale | canonical | living | persuasive | 180d | gtm |
| `release-notes` | Customer-facing release notes / changelog entry | curated | record | explanatory | derived — none | gtm |
| `retrospective` | Cycle or process retrospective — facts, insights, owned action items. One production incident is an `incident-record` in `operations/` instead | curated | record | explanatory | derived — none | governance |
| `risk-register` | Tabular risk register — per-risk probability, impact, owner, mitigation, residual, status | curated | living | explanatory | 90d | governance |
| `sales-playbook` | Sales-enablement playbook — process, methodology, qualification, plays, objection handling, collateral | curated | living | persuasive | 180d | gtm |
| `support-guide` | Goal-oriented how-to / troubleshooting article for an already-competent user — prerequisites, task steps, verification | curated | living | explanatory | 180d | operations |
| `training-guide` | Training / enablement material — objectives, content, worked examples, practice, assessment | curated | living | explanatory | 365d | gtm |
| `value-proposition` | Product positioning & value proposition — target customers, jobs/pains/gains, differentiation, messaging | canonical | living | persuasive | 180d | product |
| `redirect` | Stub pointing to archived/moved page | derived | — | — | never | — (universal, one per sub-wiki) |
| `index` | Per-sub-wiki content catalog (infra) | derived | — | — | never | — (universal, one per sub-wiki) |
| `log` | Append-only operation log (infra) | derived | — | — | never | — (universal, one per sub-wiki) |

`index` and `log` are infrastructure types — required in every sub-wiki, exempt from freshness lint and from the `authorship` required-field rule (regenerated by the wiki's scaffold step and by reindexing).

**Per-type required-field additions** (on top of the base set — `title`, `type`, `created`, `updated`, `owner`, `authorship`): `derived` pages (`source-summary`, `comparison`, `synthesis`) require non-empty `sources`. `study` is derived but exempt from the non-empty `sources` rule — the investigation itself is the source, captured in the `method` frontmatter field and the optional `raw-artifact` field. `redirect` pages require `target`, `archived`, `reason` in addition to the base set (`owner` and `authorship` still required; `created`/`updated` inherited from the archived page). `product-module` pages require `audience` in addition to the base set (`customer` | `internal`; controls who the module serves). `operational-resource`, `workspace`, `persona` and `product-module` pages require `kind`, each in a vocabulary its own type declares in `page-types.json`'s `fieldVocab` — one field name over per-type vocabularies, so no type's values are legal on another. On a `product-module` it names the module's role, held to its placement per `wiki-page-placement`. `data-model-entity` and `system-entity` pages require `instance-scope` (`tenant` | `user` | `global`; who owns the entity's instances), except an abstract entity (`abstract: true`), which has no instances and carries none. `test-scenario` pages require `verifies` — a dash-list of `[[…]]` links naming **exactly one subject**, drawn from the set its `tier` admits (integration → a `flows/` link; e2e → a `features/` link, or exactly `design-system` or `app-base`; component → a `components/` link, or a `layout-patterns/` link, a subject kind of its own). One across the whole set, not one per kind. A flow-subject page may additionally link the feature that realizes the flow, which must list that flow under its `## Task flows`. `tier` is required too, by the template and by `requires` alike (`wiki-structure-fields`' `tier` row). `ui-surface` pages require `feature`, `flows`, and `platforms`. The fields the design types add are in `wiki-design-fields`. A page stamped below `template-version: 2` is not yet required to carry `kind` and `platforms` (`information-architecture`) or `actor` and `scenario` (`user-journey`) (`wiki-template-propagation` § Template propagation). `ui-surface-impl` pages require `feature`, `implements` and `platforms`. The substrate types (`system-component`, `api-contract`, `integration`, `ui-component`, `algorithm`) and `design-system` and `layout-pattern` require `realizes` — a dash-list of `[[product:…]]` links naming the feature(s)/module the page realizes (many-to-many; e.g. `realizes:\n  - "[[product:features/<module>/<feature-slug>]]"`). Infra pages (pages that serve the system generally rather than one feature) attribute instead to the product's `app-base` page, `[[product:app-base]]`. `ui-component` pages also require `status`, except on a page stamped below `template-version: 2` (`wiki-template-propagation` § Template propagation).

**Per-type optional-field additions.** `feature` and `product-module` pages may carry `depends-on:` — a dash-list of `[[product:features/<module>/<feature-slug>]]` / `[[product:modules/<module>]]` / `[[product:app-base]]` links naming hard build-order prerequisites (e.g. `depends-on:\n  - "[[product:features/<module>/<feature-slug>]]"`). This is distinct from `related:` (`wiki-page-spec`'s general cross-reference field, constrained by the reference-hierarchy rules in `wiki-federation-model` and ordered per its own authoring convention, but not scoped to build-order semantics). The intra-wiki domain-prefix shorthand (`wiki-conventions`) applies here too. Each edge follows the composition direction `wiki-page-placement` states, which `/wiki-lint` checks. Downstream tooling consumes `depends-on:` to compute a leveled build-dependency ordering and its transpose — what each page is a prerequisite for. `ui-surface` and `ui-component` pages may additionally carry `artifacts` — a dash-list of `"kind:target"` strings pointing at the canonical visual — a Figma or Storybook URL, or a `file:` path relative to the project root to a file with no comment syntax; the `kind` vocab and shape are defined in `wiki-page-spec` (validated when present via the `artifact-kind` applicability vocab, and a `file:` target checked to exist and checked for its format). It is optional on both types — not listed in either type's `requires`. `system-component` and `integration` pages may carry `uses:` — a dash-list of `[[engineering:system-components/<name>]]` / `[[engineering:integrations/<name>]]` links naming the components and integrations the page depends on at runtime (e.g. `uses:\n  - "[[engineering:system-components/<name>]]"`). The list is the page's dependency edges; its `## Dependencies` section keeps how and why each is used. Cycles are allowed. `data-model-entity` and `system-entity` pages may carry `abstract: true`, marking an entity that defines common fields and has no instances, and `common-fields:` — a dash-list of `[[<domain>:<path>]]` links naming the abstract entities whose fields the entity carries (e.g. `common-fields:\n  - "[[product:entities/<module>/<name>]]"`). Neither is listed in a type's `requires`. A page recording a decision — `adr`, `daci-record`, `design-system`, `ui-component`, `ui-surface`, `information-architecture`, `operational-resource` — may carry `invalidates:`, a dash-list of `[[<domain>:<path>]]` links naming the live pages the decision makes **partly** stale. Targets must be pages of a `living` type: a record is superseded whole via `superseded-by`, not partly invalidated. `/wiki-lint` warns while a target's `updated` predates the declaring page's, and `_derived/cited-by.md` labels the inbound edge — which is how the invalidated page's reader reaches a decision it may not cite.

`information-architecture` pages may carry `includes:` — a dash-list of the skeleton and part pages the page composes, each an `information-architecture` page, with no cycle among them.

`information-architecture` pages may carry `journeys:` — a dash-list of the journeys an application page is designed for, each a `user-journey` page.

`information-architecture` pages may carry `layout-patterns:` — a dash-list of the layout patterns the page follows, the shell's among them, each a `layout-pattern` page.

`user-journey` pages require `actor:` — a link to the one actor the journey follows, a `persona` page or a `domain-object` page — and `scenario:`, what the actor sets out to do; the title joins the two (`wiki-design-fields`).

`design-system` pages may carry `icon-catalog:` — a link to a `catalog` page in `design`.
